Single continuous cinematic camera move, no cuts. Cinematic photorealistic live-action hybrid footage, vertical 9:16, shallow depth of field, real textures. Smooth, graceful, slow camera motion, subtle parallax. Absolutely no text, no captions, no logos, no lettering or writing on any object. The camera continues the exact same slow, steady, perfectly straight forward drift it was already in, gliding in under a pergola wrapped in warm string lights, where a young adult host in his 20s carries a big birthday cake topped with lit sparklers to the long table while a lively circle of young adult friends in their 20s and 30s around the table cheer and clap. The three CRASHERS — small toddler-sized creatures whose bodies are simple ROUND hooded onesies, soft round hooded baby-suit silhouettes, NOT shaped like bolts or diamonds or splats, the patterns only the FABRIC PRINT of each onesie: one onesie in orange fabric with a yellow zigzag print, one in blue fabric with a purple diamond print, one in green fabric with a multicolor paint-splatter print, each with a pale round face peeking out of its snug hood, big sparkly jewel-like eyes, rosy round blush cheeks, a tiny happy smile, and a red-and-white striped cone party hat on top of the hood — bounce excitedly at the table edge, one proudly holding up a stack of paper plates. Starry stays well back among the standing adults off to the side of the table, near the Crashers, exactly person-sized — the same height as the adult guests — and as the camera pushes in tighter and tighter on the cake and candles he keeps retreating further back and further to the side, well outside the camera's forward line of sight, so that by the tightest candle close-up shot no part of him at all — no face, no eyes, no mouth, no hat, no gloved hand, no fabric-arm, nothing — enters the top, sides, or any edge of frame; that tightest close-up is filled only by the cake, the candles, their sparkler and flames, and the blurred hands/shoulders of the nearest seated or standing adults, with empty out-of-focus background above the cake, never a giant golden star shape looming overhead or behind it; he is never positioned behind the cake, never above the cake, never blocks or looms over the cake or candles, never fills or enters the frame during the close-up, never larger, never towering, never closer to the camera than the people. No cloud or clubhouse is in frame. In the final second, all motion eases and the camera settles into a slow, steady, perfectly straight forward drift facing the cake table, holding on the candlelight, ready to continue.
Every human being in the scene is a young adult in their 20s or 30s — absolutely no human children, no babies, no toddlers, no minors, no middle-aged people, no elderly people, nobody with gray hair, no small human figures of any kind anywhere in frame or background; the only child-sized figures allowed are the three vinyl-toy Crasher mascots in their hooded onesies.
